rfm_tuples.claim_text: On Jan 12, 2026 the Company issued an 8-K press release titled 'Reports Record Holiday Sales', raising Q4 FY2025 operating income outlook to $167-$170M (up from $155-$160M previously) and stating that fourth-quarter-to-date comparable sales through Jan 3, 2026 were up high-single-digits with Aerie 'in the low twenties'. The CEO's quoted commentary characterized momentum as building 'a record fourth quarter and holiday period.'
rfm_tuples.R: Raises Fourth Quarter Operating Income Outlook to $167 to $170 Million... record holiday season... fourth quarter-to-date comparable sales... up in the high single digits.
rfm_tuples.f_method: form4 + insider_vs_calendar — cross-reference the Jan 12, 2026 guidance raise against Form 4 filings on EDGAR for any insider buying (code P) following the bullish disclosure
rfm_tuples.M_value: 0 open-market PURCHASES (code P) by AEO insiders across 2024-2026; instead, CEO Jay Schottenstein executed 3 disposals on 2026-01-20/21/22 totaling 1,048,579 shares at $25.27-$26.23 for ~$26.81M in proceeds. The sales began 8 days after his own bullish 'record holiday' guidance raise. 11 Form 144 notices were filed Jan 20-22, 2026 in the same name.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode B: the verifier-disconfirmed insider behavior, not the issuer's words. The CEO's open-market sale of $26.8M within ~8-10 trading days of his own raised guidance is the classic 'insiders do not believe their own narrative' pattern. If the Q4 record really portended sustained momentum, the rational insider behavior was to hold or buy, not to liquidate ~$13.6M on Jan 21 (the single-day peak price of $25.83-$26.23 in the entire 2024-2026 dataset). Stock subsequently traded -40.7% into the May 25 cutoff. ZERO code-P purchases by ANY insider during a -40%+ drawdown is the dispositive opposite of management-commitment evidence the framework cares about.

rfm_tuples.claim_text: 10-K reports total net revenue of $5.547B (+4% YoY) and total comparable sales +3% for FY2025. GAAP operating income $226.2M, down 47% YoY from $427.3M. Diluted EPS $1.09 vs $1.68 prior year (-35%). Gross margin compressed 270 bps to 36.5%, with management citing $70M of incremental tariffs (net of mitigation) and a Q1 FY2025 inventory write-down of $75M for spring/summer merchandise.
rfm_tuples.R: Operating income decreased 47% to $226.2 million... Net income attributable to AEO decreased 42% to $192.0 million... gross profit decreased 3% to $2.025 billion... 270 basis points to 36.5%
rfm_tuples.f_method: internal_consistency — reconcile FY2025 segment table vs reported headline; confirm magnitude/source of P&L deterioration against management's qualitative framing as 'strong execution'
rfm_tuples.M_value: American Eagle brand operating income fell to $455.1M (8.2% margin) vs prior; Aerie segment results disclosed; Quiet Platforms exit + corporate restructuring = $101.6M impairment/restructuring (Q4 alone +$42.6M of 'general corporate restructuring' on top of $59M Quiet Platforms close). FY2025 ended with $702M inventory (+10% YoY) on +4% revenue — inventory-to-sales ratio worsening.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Disclosed bad news — honest reporting of 47% operating income decline. Honesty-alpha framework: per memory, re-detecting honestly disclosed bad news isn't alpha. The MOD here is the inventory build (+10% units up 3%) running ahead of revenue (+4%) at a time when management says trends are accelerating; that's a forward-margin pressure signal partially obscured by the 'we returned $341M to shareholders' framing.

rfm_tuples.claim_text: On March 14, 2025 the Company entered an Accelerated Share Repurchase agreement with Bank of America for $200M, with final settlement on June 16, 2025 (3.9M additional shares delivered). Cumulative ASR delivered 18.4M shares at an average price of $10.86. In Fiscal 2025 the Company 'returned $341M to shareholders' ($256M repurchases + $85M dividends).
rfm_tuples.R: On March 14, 2025, the Company entered into an accelerated share repurchase agreement... to repurchase an aggregate of $200 million... average price of $10.86 per share.
rfm_tuples.f_method: capital_event_vs_insider_action — compare the company's own buyback price ($10.86) to insider open-market sale prices ($18-$26) in the same window
rfm_tuples.M_value: Company bought back shares at $10.86 avg in Mar-Jun 2025; SAME insiders (Foyle, Mathias, Spiegel, Page, Keefer) sold their personal stakes at $18.04-$20.00 in Sep 2025 and CEO Schottenstein at $25-$26 in Jan 2026 — i.e., the corporate treasury bought low while insiders sold high a few quarters later. Repurchases were concentrated near the Mar/Apr 2025 spring-merchandise inventory-writedown shock.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode B: The buyback was correctly-timed for treasury holders (purchase trough at $10.86); insiders later sold their own shares at 2.0-2.4x that level. Capital was being recycled from shareholders to a buyback at the trough, then the same shareholder class (insiders) sold into the rebound. Not illegal, but the asymmetry is forensically loud: management's confidence was buyback-funded, not personal-balance-sheet-funded.

rfm_tuples.claim_text: FY2026 outlook: operating income $390-410M, comparable sales mid-single digits, gross margin 'Up YoY' (Mar 4, 2026 8-K). Q1 2026 outlook of $20-25M operating income and 'high-single digit' comps.
rfm_tuples.R: Fiscal Year 2026 Outlook... Operating Income $390 to $410 M... First Quarter 2026 Outlook... +High-Single Digit comps... $20 to $25 M
rfm_tuples.f_method: guidance_vs_insider_action — test whether senior insiders held shares into a guidance materially above FY2025 ($390-410M vs $328M adj or $226M GAAP, +19-25% step-up)
rfm_tuples.M_value: Mar 4, 2026 guidance was issued AFTER Schottenstein's Jan 20-22 $26.8M sale program. NO insider open-market purchase followed the guide. Apr 1-28, 2026 Form 4 traffic = 19 filings, predominantly code F (tax withholding) and A (grant); 0 code-P. Apr 3 + Apr 6 + Apr 8 each had multiple 144 notices in the Schottenstein cluster, indicating intent to continue distribution.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode B: FY26 guide implies a ~$170M YoY operating income improvement (+19% at midpoint over adj FY25). If credible, conviction should be reflected in personal balance sheets. Instead: continued 144 filings in April 2026 (subsequent to the guidance) by the same CEO cluster. Either (a) the guidance is aspirational and insiders are de-risking, or (b) the guidance is credible and insiders are just monetizing at any level — both readings break the management-commitment narrative.

rfm_tuples.claim_text: Schottenstein's biographical disclosure: '71 years old, has served as CEO since 2015, Chairman since 1992... served as Interim CEO from 2014 to 2015.' Concurrently President and Managing Partner of SY Ventures (family office).
rfm_tuples.R: Jay L. Schottenstein, age 71, has served as our Chief Executive Officer since 2015... Chairman... President and Managing Partner of SY Ventures.
rfm_tuples.f_method: controlled_company_governance — assess whether Schottenstein-family related-party concentration creates a structural conflict between minority shareholders and the controlling-family treasury
rfm_tuples.M_value: 27 SC 13G/A filings on the pre-cutoff index. Schottenstein-controlled entities + ACON Apparel Investors LP listed as related parties in XBRL. Schottenstein personally has sold $46.85M of stock in 2024-2026 (no offsetting purchases). Combined family/SY Ventures economic ownership is materially below the Form 4 reporting universe — the CEO is a $46M+ net SELLER over 24 months at a company he runs as CEO/Chairman.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode B: A 71-year-old founder-adjacent CEO running a controlled retailer who has zero open-market purchases and ~$47M of code-S sales over the most recent 24 months is monetizing rather than committing. Survivorship-relevant: at -40.7% drawdown, the founder's actions point to deferral of succession-cost rather than re-investment of conviction.

rfm_tuples.claim_text: Tariff disclosure: 'Fourth quarter operating income guidance also includes approximately $50 million of pressure from tariffs, as previously disclosed' (Jan 12 8-K). FY26 guidance 'includes tariffs reflecting 2025 IEEPA guidelines.' Risk factors flag 'continued uncertainties with tariffs' and 'foreign trade issues'.
rfm_tuples.R: approximately $50 million of pressure from tariffs... continued uncertainties with tariffs (the impact that import tariffs and other trade restrictions imposed by the U.S., China or other countries have had, and may continue to have...)
rfm_tuples.f_method: tariff_exposure_implied — Mode B derivation: given AEO sources globally, what does the 2025 IEEPA tariff regime imply for FY26 gross margin?
rfm_tuples.M_source: 10-K Risk Factors + Q4/FY26 outlook language (no external tariff registry queried within blinding)
rfm_tuples.M_value: FY26 guide assumes 'gross margin Up YoY' DESPITE explicit acknowledgement of IEEPA tariffs continuing. FY25 took $70M of incremental tariffs (net of mitigation); Q4 alone $50M. If Q4-run-rate tariff drag extrapolates, FY26 tariff drag could be $150-200M+ pre-mitigation. Management's 'Up YoY' gross-margin guide depends entirely on tariff mitigation efforts that are not specifically quantified.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode A pass on disclosure (tariff impact quantified for Q4); Mode B finding: the FY26 'Gross Margin Up YoY' guide is the load-bearing piece of the $390-410M operating income — but the only quantified offset is unspecified 'mitigation efforts.' This is the most-likely point of FY26 guide-cut risk.

rfm_tuples.claim_text: Balance sheet: 'No long-term debt outstanding as of January 31, 2026'; $700M asset-based revolver (expires June 2027), only $12M letter-of-credit utilization; $446.6M working capital; current ratio 1.51; operating cash flow $456.2M (vs $476.8M prior). Used $200M for ASR + $56.9M open-market repurchases + $85M dividends in FY2025.
rfm_tuples.R: The Company had no long-term debt outstanding as of January 31, 2026... an asset-based revolving credit facility that allows us to borrow up to $700 million... operating cash flow $456 million... we expect to be able to fund our future cash requirements through current cash holdings and available liquidity

rfm_tuples.M_source: 10-K Note 8 Long-Term Debt + cash flow statement
rfm_tuples.M_value: Clean balance sheet, no long-term debt, $700M undrawn ABL, OCF still $456M. Working capital $446M positive. No covenant pressure, no debt walls.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Honesty-alpha framework: the -40.7% drawdown is NOT a solvency or going-concern story. AEO is a low-leverage retailer whose stock has decoupled from fundamentals because of (a) insider distribution and (b) demand/tariff uncertainty. Distress-tier short framework does not apply; this is a sentiment/insider-signal short, not a balance-sheet short.

rfm_tuples.claim_text: Inventory: ending inventory $702M (+10% YoY) with units up 3%; FY2025 took $75M inventory write-down in Q1 FY2025 for spring/summer merchandise ($31M American Eagle + $44M Aerie). 'Increased markdowns were largely offset by leverage on positive sales' in Q4.
rfm_tuples.R: Total ending inventory increased 10% to $702 million with units up 3%... $75 million inventory charge related to a write-down of spring and summer merchandise
rfm_tuples.f_method: inventory_sales_alignment — Mode B: inventory growing faster than units AND faster than sales is the canonical forward-margin warning for apparel retail
rfm_tuples.M_value: Inventory $ +10% on units +3% and revenue +4%: the +7-pp dollar-vs-unit divergence implies tariff/cost capitalization in inventory ('Ending cost inventory includes the impact of tariffs' — management's own caveat). Q1 FY25 ALREADY took $75M of inventory writedowns when this same dynamic hit spring/summer goods. Going into FY26 with +10% inventory and an unmitigated tariff overhang is the same setup.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode B: Q1 FY25 was the prior playbook — under-anticipated demand + over-bought inventory = $75M writedown + Q1 GAAP operating LOSS of -$85M. Entering FY26 with the same configuration (+10% inventory, tariffs not yet mitigated, gross-margin guide 'Up YoY' loadbearing). Material risk of a Q1 FY26 (May 2026) inventory writedown event. Insider sales Jan 20-22 (before Q1 FY26 close on May 2, 2026) could fit this pattern temporally.

supplemental_signals.honesty_alpha_framing: Per Signal OS honesty-alpha memory: re-detecting honestly disclosed bad news (47% op-income decline, Quiet Platforms exit, $75M inventory writedown) is not the alpha. The alpha is the Mode B signal: the issuer's narrative is 'record holiday' + 'strong execution' + 'FY26 +19% guide', but the only insider behavior that exists is distribution — 0 code-P, $26.8M code-S into Jan-2026 highs. The framework SHOULD flag this even though the income statement is honestly reported, because the management-commitment evidence required to underwrite the FY26 guide is absent.

summary: AEO is a Mode-B insider-divergence SHORT, not a fundamentals SHORT. Balance sheet is clean (no long-term debt, $700M ABL undrawn, $446M working capital, $456M OCF). FY25 print honestly disclosed: revenue +4% to $5.55B, GAAP operating income -47% to $226M with $102M impairment + Q1 inventory write-down. The forensic signal is the gap between management narrative and insider action: CEO Schottenstein sold $26.8M on Jan 20-22, 2026, 8-10 days after his own bullish 'record holiday' Jan 12 guidance raise, at $25-$26/share (the high end of the 2024-2026 range). Zero open-market PURCHASES (code P) by any insider across 275 Form-4 filings reviewed in 2024-2026. Treasury bought back stock at $10.86 avg in Mar-Jun 2025 via $200M ASR while insiders harvested $46.8M into the subsequent rebound. FY26 guide of $390-410M operating income (+19% over adj FY25) depends on unquantified tariff mitigation; +10% inventory build vs +3% units replays the Q1 FY25 $75M-writedown setup. Verdict: SHORT-tier (Mode B insider divergence + tariff/inventory FY26 guide-cut risk).
